## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs fixing before merge. It stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks up the lower-cased key, so the new method breaks for any key that contains an uppercase letter. The rest of the change (the TTL value with its matching comment, and the expiry test) has no defects in the scope this review covered.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the key exactly as given while `get` (app/cache.py:17) reads `self._store.get(key.lower())`. The class comment at app/cache.py:14-15 states the rule this breaks: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` (tests/test_cache.py:10-14) only calls `set` with the lowercase key `"alpha"`, so it passes even with this bug. Fix: change the line to `self._store[key.lower()] = (...)`, and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"` and reads it back with `get("Alpha")` and `get("alpha")`. — Any caller that passes a mixed-case key to the new public `set` API gets permanent cache misses with no error. Those entries also pile up in `_store` and are never read or removed, because expiry deletion only happens inside `get` on the lower-cased key.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` replaces `time.monotonic` with a controlled clock, so the expiry test is deterministic and doesn't sleep. This works because app/cache.py calls `time.monotonic()` through the module attribute.
- The `DEFAULT_TTL` comment at app/cache.py:7 was updated together with the value at app/cache.py:8, so the two still agree.
